title: Learning-induced neural plasticity of speech processing before birth
scope: Prenatal exposure to selected speech-like stimuli and neonatal mismatch responses; not word comprehension, personal memories or a universal developmental effect.
claim_supported: A repeated prenatal sound exposure was associated with stronger neonatal neural responses to specified sound-feature changes.

title: Where Your Elements Came From
author_or_institution: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day
scope: Institutional explanation of hydrogen's primordial origin and stellar nuclear production of carbon and oxygen. Does not imply every atom or chemical structure formed in a star.
claim_supported: Carbon and oxygen in bodies have stellar formation histories; much bodily hydrogen derives from the early universe.

title: How the Eyes Work
scope: Light enters the eye and retinal light-sensitive cells convert it to signals conveyed toward the brain. Does not supply a theory of consciousness or complete visual recognition mechanism.
claim_supported: Seeing depends on physical light reception and signal transduction rather than an inner person viewing a literal miniature object.

title: Mechanism of phototaxis in marine zooplankton
scope: Selective eyespot illumination, adjacent ciliary beating and phototactic steering in Platynereis larvae; non-image-forming direction detection. No claim about subjective experience.
claim_supported: A simple eyespot can help guide swimming through its local coupling to ciliary activity without forming an image.

title: Temporal comparisons in bacterial chemotaxis
author_or_institution: J. E. Segall, S. M. Block and H. C. Berg
scope: Measured stimulus-response temporal weighting and adaptation mutants in tethered Escherichia coli. Functional short-term comparison is not humanlike recollection.
claim_supported: Recent chemical stimulation influences bacterial response and adaptation machinery affects that temporal comparison.

title: Whatever Does Not Kill Us: Cumulative Lifetime Adversity, Vulnerability, and Resilience
author_or_institution: Mark D. Seery, E. Alison Holman and Roxane Cohen Silver
scope: Multiyear observational study of reported lifetime adversity and selected mental-health/well-being outcomes. Does not randomize hardship, identify an individual causal optimum or license induced suffering.
claim_supported: In the studied sample, some reported prior adversity was associated with better selected outcomes than either no or high reported adversity.

title: Exact Onset and Peak Laws for Bounded Adaptive Responses
scope: Analytic model amendment distinguishing repair/damage mechanisms, actual zero-dose normalization, additive and multiplicative response laws. Threshold ordering alone is insufficient; no new biological fit or dose advice.
claim_supported: A beneficial interval requires an actual repair advantage relative to damage under the chosen model and endpoint; earlier activation alone does not guarantee it.

title: Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe
author_or_institution: Carlos López-Otín, Maria A. Blasco, Linda Partridge, Manuel Serrano and Guido Kroemer
scope: Authors' research synthesis of interrelated molecular/cellular/systemic mechanisms of ageing. Does not establish one universal reserve, a fixed individual lifespan, a treatment recommendation or an all-process theory.
claim_supported: Ageing research examines interrelated genetic damage, protein maintenance, mitochondrial function, stem-cell capacity and intercellular communication among other processes.

title: The dual process model of coping with bereavement: Rationale and description
scope: Proposed coping model distinguishing loss-oriented and restoration-oriented stressors with oscillation and respite. Descriptive theoretical framework, not a universal stage timetable, required behaviour or clinical advice.
claim_supported: An influential model describes shifts between attending to a loss and attending to changed-life tasks rather than demanding uninterrupted grief confrontation.

title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave
scope: Chapters VI and VII; author's historical autobiographical account, not invented internal narration.
claim_supported: Sophia Auld began teaching Douglass letters, Hugh Auld stopped instruction; Douglass continued learning including from boys in Baltimore and described the painful difference between understanding his condition and obtaining freedom.

title: Reconstruction of Automobile Destruction: An Example of the Interaction Between Language and Memory
author_or_institution: Elizabeth F. Loftus and John C. Palmer
scope: Original experimental article, especially experiments I and II. Does not establish that all autobiographical memory is inaccurate, or uniquely resolve every mechanism of wording effects.
claim_supported: Question wording affected reported collision speeds; in experiment II the smashed wording produced more broken-glass reports at one week than hit wording, despite absence of glass.

title: Report of the Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme
author_or_institution: Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme, Commissioner Catherine Holmes
scope: Volume 1 introductory preface and overview, especially pp. ii and xxv; specific historical findings, not current legal advice.
claim_supported: Income averaging without other evidence was an unreliable basis for entitlement/debt conclusions; recipients were treated as receiving income at times they had not, with legal and institutional failures and unreasonable burdens of producing historical records.

title: The Bounded Observer, and The Ceiling and the Constants
scope: Declared operational records and future operation/readout classes; exact retained-algebra forgetting in the finite complex model. Human memory is an interpretive application, not proved to implement that channel.
claim_supported: Retention adequacy depends on the questions and operations supported. A summary that merges histories with different admitted future readings is insufficient for that declared task.

title: The Structural Integrity of Daddy Pig: A Treatise on Bounded Confidence
scope: Author-owned satire and voice reference. Fictional character interpretation; invented mock statistics and systems analogies are not scientific evidence.
claim_supported: The author has written affectionately and satirically about the character's confidence. This essay develops the distinction between confidence to attempt and evidence-sensitive correction without reproducing mock statistical claims.

title: The Bounded Observer and current project operational definitions
scope: Declared record sufficiency relative to allowed future operations/readings. Interpretive use in human choice is not a proof of moral law, free will or a universal brain update mechanism.
claim_supported: A retained description must preserve history distinctions that change the admitted future readings or actions it is intended to support.

title: On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, second edition
scope: Primary historical account, especially Broad Street household/water investigation and Snow's caution about attributing outbreak decline to handle removal. Does not itself establish modern microbiological mechanisms or provide current treatment advice.
claim_supported: Snow investigated water usage and illness distribution; the handle was removed, but he recorded that attacks had declined beforehand and could not establish whether the well remained infectious at removal.

title: Exact Onset and Peak Laws for Bounded Adaptive Responses; proposed hormesis correction
scope: Exact deductions within specified response models and correction of earlier unrestricted necessity/universal-peak claims. Author-proposed correction, not an issued journal corrigendum; SSRN submissions await completeness review as of 13 October 2026.
claim_supported: Boundedness alone does not force a beneficial interval; corrected onset/peak conclusions require the chosen repair/harm model and endpoint assumptions.

title: Cargo Cult Science
author_or_institution: Richard P. Feynman; Caltech commencement address
scope: Primary address on scientific integrity and self-deception. It is an argument about scientific practice, not an empirical demonstration that all people reason in one way.
claim_supported: Feynman urged scientists to guard against self-deception and disclose weaknesses or contrary information instead of presenting only the favorable account.

title: The Geometry of Bounded Records
scope: Sections 1–4 and 8: finite cone model, named classification premises, positive trace readings, binary projective geometry and canonical filter action.
claim_supported: Amounts and normalized readings have different roles; the stated record/filter model supplies hyperbolic projective geometry. Boundedness or an associative curve alone does not select it. The map/ruler/sofa examples are analogies, not additional deductions.

title: Light Time and Horizons
scope: Sections 1–5: event/signal/clock bridges, Lorentz comparison, proper versus received clocks, distinct sky measures and the acceleration-horizon criterion.
claim_supported: The physical event identification gives the conformal Lorentz metric; the specified calibrated clock model gives proper time form. Direction probability, local photon density and radiation energy are different records. A horizon depends on the traversal law as well as the geometric path. Different physical schedules can change an observer trajectory; relabelling the same trajectory with new clock units cannot create a physical horizon.

title: Two Observers
scope: Sections 1–5 and 7: declared complex composition, purification/dilation, determinant and concurrence identities, correlation writing, retained-algebra selection and finite-GKSL-exposure boundary bound.
claim_supported: Pure joint states can have mixed marginals; local irreversibility can result from discarding an environment; correlations can be written without pure marginals. Entanglement/mass correspondence requires the momentum dictionary. Full-rank boundary exclusion concerns finite integrated exposure in the stated model, not finite duration alone.

title: The Bounded Observer
scope: Parts I–V and X, especially operational closure Theorem 1.
claim_supported: Finite complex records, effects, instruments, composites and marginals close under the named operations, purification and environment dilation. Physical applications supply additional bridges. This source also supports the unmarked closure exposition later in the article.

title: The Partner Freedom
scope: Sections 1–8: marginal versus joint invariance, declared local frames, connection/holonomy, additional dynamics, Higgs stabilizer and anomaly-free charges within a declared matter family.
claim_supported: A genuine local frame redundancy admits comparison via a connection; a physical action remains additional. Matter/charge consequences are conditional on the specified representation and interaction premises, not derived actual particle content from bare boundedness.

title: Where Singularities Can Live
scope: Sections 1–7 and 9–10: bounded values versus gradients; global hyperbolic and mixed-qubit heat-flow results on stated sources; normalized sphere bubbling; regularization constructions and fluid Conjecture 12.
claim_supported: Specified interior models remain regular; specified spherical flows can concentrate. Conditions include target metric, source geometry, PDE, initial data and energy convention. Fluid pressure closure does not prove global regularity. Human grief/rigidity passages are explicitly philosophical images, not applications proved here. The mixed-state smoothing statement is explicitly for two-level quantum states with a positive initial margin from purity. The hyperbolic and mixed two-level smoothing statements retain a fixed compact flat source without boundary and their stated initial-data conditions.

title: Gravity as Equilibrium
scope: Sections 1–6 and 8: separate stationary and thermodynamic routes, ergosurface/event-horizon distinction, patch completion under named assumptions and non-equilibrium scope.
claim_supported: Stationary vacuum Einstein reduction contains a coupled hyperbolic Ernst target; the thermodynamic route has independent horizon premises. A stationary patch can fail at an ergosurface without a curvature singularity. Equilibrium derivation does not finish microscopic quantum gravity or determine cosmic parameters.

title: Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State
scope: Primary 1995 paper abstract and publication record opened directly; full scope reconciled with current Paper 7. Horizon-area entropy, Unruh temperature and all-local-horizon Clausius equilibrium yield Einstein's equation.
claim_supported: The short named-Jacobson paragraph attributes the conditional thermodynamic route to its established primary source. It does not adopt a proof that gravity needs no quantum description.

title: The Ernst equation and ergosurfaces
author_or_institution: Piotr T. Chrusciel, Gert-Martin Greuel, Reinhard Meinel and Sebastian J. Szybka
scope: Primary paper abstract and publication record opened directly; smooth Ernst potential and finite-order zero hypotheses match the current Paper 7 imported completion theorem.
claim_supported: A singular-looking stationary reduction can reconstruct a smooth spacetime near the relevant ergosurface under its stated assumptions. This is not removal of all physical curvature singularities.

title: The Ceiling and the Constants
scope: Sections 2–5 and 7: fixed-constraint readouts, implementable retained-algebra selection, residual dynamics and same-fibre physical completion criterion.
claim_supported: Law-fixed readings, data-dependent readings and missing model content can be distinguished across declared admissible completions. Operational closure does not uniquely select actual constants, readout operators, physical preparation or generators.

title: IDA and StateAtlas: current instruments and operational contract
author_or_institution: Daniel John Murray / The Bounded Observer programme
scope: Current research tools, two distinct prototypes, declared signals/feature maps and independent read/action gate.
claim_supported: IDA asks which measurements change a useful future action. Instruments exist; physiological interpretation and added usefulness remain unvalidated. The article's opening person/instrument is a hypothetical question, not a clinical result.

title: The Bounded Observer
scope: Parts I–V and IX–X, operational closure Theorem 1, sufficient records and declared physical application recipe.
claim_supported: Record sufficiency is relative to declared future operations/readings; finite complex model operations close as a loop; applications need their observation and intervention bridges. No closed theory of all physical history is asserted.

title: Arc Virtual Cell Challenge: dated competition results and candidate-family review
author_or_institution: Daniel John Murray / retained author and official server records
scope: 31-EchoFull recorded validation-panel outcome observed 10 October 2026; retained official/author result provenance; separate later candidate family and submission outcomes.
claim_supported: The non-neural rule-based empirical-source predictor EchoFull held rank 221 among 1,416 validation-panel entries in the author-preserved official result observed 10 October 2026. It is a dated validation result, not final standing. Later fitted variants and rejected candidates retain separate outcomes. No accuracy percentage, universal superiority or all-physics validation is claimed.

title: Observatory cell-response flights
author_or_institution: Daniel John Murray / The Bounded Observer programme
scope: Two earlier Observatory flights with separate protocols and failed added-candidate success gates.
claim_supported: The earlier cellular experiments are distinct from the Arc competition and retain their failures. The article does not treat these results as failed versions of the successful Arc entry or as independent replication of it.

title: Scientific AI and retained evidence
author_or_institution: Daniel John Murray / The Bounded Observer programme
scope: Typed evidence, source versions, dependencies, authorizations, finite tools and Active Context's first tied comparison.
claim_supported: Warrant-preserving memory is an engineering task with explicit evidential objects. Active Context tied the comparator rather than proving a performance advantage. The proposed benefits of a source-aware assistant remain prospective and measurable.

title: Exact Onset and Peak Laws for Bounded Adaptive Responses
scope: Sections 1–6: amendment of unrestricted necessity/peak statements, exact control calibration, three distinct conditional response laws and independently measured components.
claim_supported: Threshold ordering and boundedness alone do not guarantee benefit. Corrected exact laws depend on repair/harm components, actual baseline and specified model. The amendment provides no new biological fit, treatment recommendation or issued journal corrigendum.

title: T15 and T15b historical protocols/results; current capstone empirical-status table
author_or_institution: Daniel John Murray / historical programme analyses
scope: Capstone IX and byte-preserved provenance protocols/outputs: original locally frozen criteria failed; later fitted-clock analysis exploratory; present revision did not independently rerun every empirical pipeline.
claim_supported: The earlier population comparisons, with protocols frozen locally before decisive analysis, missed their criteria. An exploratory clock revision does not change that outcome. The article reports retained research history, not a fresh data analysis.

title: Arithmetic and predictive records
author_or_institution: Daniel John Murray / The Bounded Observer programme
scope: Divisibility records, exact projection/refinement and independent requirements for actual-prime approximations.
claim_supported: The arithmetic branch shares the sufficient-record/refinement question. Exact identities differ from controlled prime prediction; arithmetic refinement index is not physical time and primes are not asserted to be quantum fields.

title: The Bounded Observer research lab and research tasks
author_or_institution: Daniel John Murray / The Bounded Observer programme
scope: Concrete question/model/comparison/check/result/revision cycle; runnable models; current tasks with declared loss conditions and source attribution.
claim_supported: Future work is specified rather than promised. Examples of improved diagnosis, access or tools are philosophical prospects requiring material arrangements and independent validation.
